A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAPS study. The full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; v4 retains appendices A-C and adds Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original consultation-history analysis and ranking, retrieval, ablation, and sensitivity experiments on Commercial and Amazon data.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the performance comparisons and supplementary analyses in Tables 2-8.

M1.justification: The ID-text fusion, MoAE pooling, general alignment, personalized alignment, losses, and inference procedure are unchanged. Correcting 'MEPS' to 'MAPS' in the parameter description is a naming correction.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Commercial and Amazon ranking evaluations and Commercial retrieval evaluation. The new consultation examples illustrate these existing datasets without adding tasks or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 2-4: the six personalized-search baselines, BM25/BGE-M3/CHIQ retrieval comparators, and SESRec/UnifiedSSR/UniSAR multi-scenario comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B.2 preserve the splits, metrics, 99-negative ranking evaluation, all-item retrieval evaluation, training budgets, and model settings. Appendix D documents access and examples without revising experimental procedures.

E4.justification: The component and representation ablations, scalability experiments, threshold sensitivity, and activation comparisons in Tables 5-8 and Figure 4 are unchanged. Figures 5-6 contain dataset examples, without new evaluated case studies or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the paired t-tests at p < 0.05 and the same significance markers. Neither repeated-run or seed information nor uncertainty-reporting practices change.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and findings in Tables 1-8 and Figures 2 and 4 are unchanged. For example, Commercial MAPS NDCG@10 remains 0.4359 and retrieval MRR@10 remains 0.3805. The new dialogues are illustrative data, not performance results.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, pooling equations, alignment objectives, and mathematical reasoning are retained. The model-name correction does not revise any definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same motivation-modeling contribution, architectural claims, and claimed retrieval/ranking advantages. Adding a code-availability sentence does not alter the scientific claims.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Section 7's methodological limitations are unchanged. Appendix D newly states that Commercial data cannot currently be released because of policy and legal restrictions, clarifying a limitation on independent replication.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-repository link in the abstract, an Amazon-data download link in Appendix D, an explicit Commercial-data access restriction, and example consultations. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and licensing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and positioning relative to personalized search, conversational retrieval, and joint search/recommendation research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 appends a short Dataset Details section, updates author/contact and contribution footnotes, and corrects 'MEPS' to 'MAPS'. The main narrative and existing section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures 5-6 showing Amazon and privacy-redacted Commercial consultation dialogues. The abstract and final appendix page undergo limited reflow; existing figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency through explicit code/data access information, disclosure of Commercial-data restrictions, and concrete consultation examples. These are useful but limited gains: the scientific methods and evidence are unchanged, and the supplied PDFs do not establish the completeness or usability of the linked resources.
